title: Variant slice prober: lightweight toolcall diff harness and rollback suggester
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: During canary / A/B / shadow rollouts we need a fast, low-cost way to detect function-call / structured-output incompatibilities that matter to downstream apps. Existing approaches either run expensive full-evals or flag noise (minor ordering/whitespace diffs). Goal: build a lightweight prober that samples variant slices, computes per-function compatibility scores, and surfaces actionable rollback suggestions (per-customer and global). Scope includes runtime probes, a small offline scoring service, and Console surface for slices and recommended actions.
acceptance_criteria: Prober runs against shadow traffic with configurable weight and returns per-function compatibility scores within 3 minutes of batch completion
Define and implement at least three heuristics: structural shape-change rate, missing-action-rate, and enum-value-drift score
Console shows top-10 divergent slices with traffic %, sample examples, and suggested action (monitor / throttle / rollback)
Auto-rollback can be triggered in two modes: suggested (manual approve) and soft-auto (auto-unwind after configurable threshold), with audit log entries
Telemetry emitted: shape_change_rate, unknown_action_rate, per_function_diff_entropy; dashboards reflect these metrics within 5m of probe completion
implementation_notes: Architecture: (1) lightweight Prober component in the serving runtime that duplicates a subset of requests to a 'probe sink' and records toolcall signatures and structured outputs; (2) Probe-worker that computes slice-level diffs and scoring offline (k8s job); (3) Scoring rules stored as config (json) and evolved via PRs; (4) Console UI shows slices + suggested policy actions; (5) An orchestrator that wires suggested actions into existing rollout control plane.
progress: 2025-02-10: Spec drafted. 2025-02-14: Spike completed for in-memory probe sink; found ~12% of sampled requests for a test model produced enum drift vs baseline. 2025-02-18: Prototype probe-worker outputs per-function diff heatmaps (s3 artifacts). 2025-02-22: Security review kickoff; requested data retention limits and redaction for PII. 2025-02-25: Design review with Console team — agreed on slice list UX and action affordances. 2025-02-28: PR #12345 opened for probe-worker scoring logic (see related_links). Current blockers: infra quota for shadow sinks in dedicated stacks; need infra ticket to expand. Next: implement auto-suggest rule engine and wire audit logs for suggested rollbacks.
risks_and_tradeoffs: False positives: strict heuristics may trigger unnecessary rollbacks — mitigate by conservative thresholds and manual approval by default
Cost: shadowing and extra probe processing adds cost — mitigate by sampling slices and running scoring jobs at low frequency for low-traffic customers
Privacy: captured structured output may include user data — enforce redaction, retention policies, and opt-outs per customer
Latency: runtime duplication must be non-blocking — probe writes must be async and bounded to avoid backpressure
metrics_and_signals: shape_change_rate: percent of requests where top-level keys differ from baseline
unknown_action_rate: percent of calls invoking previously-unseen functions/actions
per_function_diff_entropy: entropy score for argument/value distributions
slice_failure_rate: percent of examples in a slice that exceed compatibility threshold
rollback_suggester_score: composite score used to recommend rollback
